title: RESOLUTION (YAROSLAVSKY - McOSKER) relative to designating locations in Council District 5 for enforcement against sitting, lying, sleeping, or storing,…
text:
[Council File 26-4118-S13; CD 5]
[Items for which Public Hearings Have Not Been Held - (10 Votes Required for Consideration)]
RESOLUTION (YAROSLAVSKY - McOSKER) relative to designating locations in Council District 5 for enforcement against sitting, lying, sleeping, or storing, using maintaining, or placing personal property, or otherwise obstructing the public right-of-way, as further detailed in the Los Angeles Municipal Code (LAMC) Section 41.18.
Recommendation(s) for Council action:
1. RESOLVE, pursuant to Section 41.18 of the LAMC, to designate the following locations for enforcement against sitting, lying, sleeping, or storing, using maintaining, or placing personal property, or otherwise obstructing the public right-of-way, up to the maximum distance and effective for the maximum period of time prescribed, and as further detailed in the LAMC.
a. 3734 Overland Avenue-School/Daycare
b. 10401 Venice Boulevard-School/Daycare
c. 8511 Beverly Place-School/Daycare
d. 989 South St. Andrews Place-Public Safety
e. 10525 Venice Boulevard-Public Safety
f. 10860 Santa Monica Boulevard-Public Safety
g. 11043 West Pico Boulevard-Public Safety
h. La Cienega Boulevard & Beverly Boulevard-Public Safety
i. Orlando Boulevard & Beverly Boulevard-Public Safety
j. 8700 Beverly Boulevard-Public Safety
k. 110 North George Burns Road-Public Safety
l. 8723 West Alden Drive-Public Safety
m. 8575 West 3rd Street-Public Safety
n. 444 South San Vicente Boulevard-Public Safety
o. 350 La Cienega Boulevard-Public Safety
2. RESOLVE to direct and authorize the City Department(s) with jurisdiction over the identified locations to post appropriate notices of the above prohibitions at these locations, and to begin enforcement upon the expiration of any required posting period
Community Impact Statement:
None submitted
summary: Council would designate 15 Council District 5 locations, mostly near schools, daycares and other public-safety sites, where the city can enforce bans on sitting, lying, sleeping or storing belongings in the public right-of-way.
